Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the

starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

---
name: continual-arc
description: Solve Continual-ARC grid puzzles; infer transformations from demos, manage attempt/demo costs, validate outputs, and format actions.
---

# Continual-ARC

1. Treat each instance as independent. Read the complete input, all demos, and current budgets. Compare input-output pairs exactly, recording what changed and what stayed fixed; distinguish observed behavior from hypotheses.
2. Use a demo request only when a plausible, targeted example can distinguish live hypotheses enough to justify its cost. Check its returned input-output pair directly against the hypotheses. Respect the cap. After an incorrect submission, treat the entire candidate as rejected: revisit the transformation and interactions rather than guessing which cells caused failure or making near-identical edits.
3. Before submission, validate the transformation against every demo, including unchanged markers and crossing/stopping/overlap cases. If the test contains an unobserved case, spend an available demo on it when informative; otherwise do not claim the detail is established. For grids with structured repeating sequences, infer each masked cell from its row/column context and verify both sides of each gap when available; do not extrapolate one convenient motif across regions with different phases or structure.
4. For large outputs, use code only as a private calculation aid: transcribe the input exactly and keep it immutable; apply the explicit rule; then verify dimensions, row lengths, values, changed-cell locations, and all required invariants. Check that the same operation reproduces every demo. On an incorrect result, audit the complete proposed grid against the input and rule before submitting again; serialization checks do not validate the rule.
5. Return exactly one supported action JSON on the last line. Submit only after rule and output checks; request_demos only within the cap; use finish only after the instance is over. Never execute a puzzle action through shell or another tool.
